draft.title: New ideas and reforms
card: an economic system where private owners run factories and businesses to make a profit. Industrial change made it grow, as owners invested in machines and hired workers for wages.
an idea that grew as a reaction to factory life. Socialists said industry should be owned or shared by the community, so that wealth is spread more fairly among workers.
a movement in Britain from the late 1830s. Its supporters wanted votes for working men, so that workers could have a say in making the laws.
laws passed by the British Parliament that began to limit working hours, especially for children and women in factories.
draft.remember: Industrial change brought new ideas about wealth and power, and laws that began to protect workers.

a.q: Which of these best describes a Chartist demand in Britain?
opts: Shorter hours for children in mills
a.why: Chartists campaigned for working men to have the vote. Shared ownership of industry is a socialist idea, and limits on children's hours came from Factory Acts, which were laws rather than a Chartist demand.
a.clue: Think about what the Chartists wanted workers to have a say in.

b.q: In 1830s Leeds, a mill owner says workers should be free to bargain for wages, and that he may keep the profits from his mill. Which idea does he support?
b.why: Private owners running a business for profit, with workers hired for wages, is capitalism. Socialism is the tempting wrong answer, because it also deals with factory wealth, but it says industry should be owned or shared by the community.
b.clue: Who owns the mill, and who gets the profit?
